classification.difficultyReason: For exactly one matching pair, choose the repeated face, the different face and the position of the different face so each ordered outcome is counted once.

content.prompt: A die is thrown 3 times. Find the probability that

answer.worked:
There are $6^3=216$ equally likely ordered outcomes. Only $(4,4,4)$ qualifies.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{three 4s})&=\frac{1}{6^3}\\P(\text{three 4s})&=\frac{1}{216}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: all three tosses are the same number.

answer.worked:
Each of the six faces gives one matching triple out of $6^3=216$ outcomes.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{all the same})&=\frac{6}{216}\\P(\text{all the same})&=\frac{1}{36}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: two 5’s are thrown and then one 2.

answer.worked:
There are three ordered outcomes, one for each position of the 2.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{two 5s and a 2})&=\frac{3}{216}\\P(\text{two 5s and a 2})&=\frac{1}{72}\end{align*}$$

The 5 has three possible positions. Each other throw has five possible faces.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{one 5})&=\frac{3\times5\times5}{216}\\P(\text{one 5})&=\frac{75}{216}\\P(\text{one 5})&=\frac{25}{72}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\frac{25}{27}$

Count the outcomes with zero 5s and with one 5.
answer.worked:
There are $5^3$ outcomes with no 5 and $3\times5^2$ outcomes with one 5. Let $A$ be the event of at most one 5.

$$\begin{align*}P(A)&=\frac{5^3+3\times5^2}{216}\\P(A)&=\frac{200}{216}\\P(A)&=\frac{25}{27}\end{align*}$$

The throw that is not a 5 can be in any of three positions and can show any of five faces.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{two 5s})&=\frac{3\times5}{216}\\P(\text{two 5s})&=\frac{15}{216}\\P(\text{two 5s})&=\frac{5}{72}\end{align*}$$

children.label: h
children.prompt: exactly two of the numbers are the same.

answer.short:
$\frac{5}{12}$

Choose the repeated face, the different face and the position of the different face.
answer.worked:
Choose the repeated face in 6 ways, the different face in 5 ways and its position in 3 ways.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly one pair})&=\frac{6\times5\times3}{216}\\P(\text{exactly one pair})&=\frac{90}{216}\\P(\text{exactly one pair})&=\frac{5}{12}\end{align*}$$

Each throw has five possible faces other than 4, giving $5^3$ outcomes with no 4.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one 4})&=1-\frac{5^3}{216}\\P(\text{at least one 4})&=\frac{216-125}{216}\\P(\text{at least one 4})&=\frac{91}{216}\end{align*}$$

The first throw can be any of six faces. To avoid repeats, there are five choices for the second and four for the third.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{all different})&=\frac{6\times5\times4}{216}\\P(\text{all different})&=\frac{120}{216}\\P(\text{all different})&=\frac{5}{9}\end{align*}$$

children.label: k
children.prompt: the middle toss of the die is a 4.

answer.worked:
The first and last throws can each be any of six faces. Only the middle throw is fixed.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{middle throw is 4})&=\frac{6\times1\times6}{216}\\P(\text{middle throw is 4})&=\frac{36}{216}\\P(\text{middle throw is 4})&=\frac{1}{6}\end{align*}$$

children.label: l
children.prompt: neither a 6 nor a 1 is thrown.

answer.worked:
Each throw can be a 2, 3, 4 or 5.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{neither 6 nor 1})&=\frac{4^3}{216}\\P(\text{neither 6 nor 1})&=\frac{64}{216}\\P(\text{neither 6 nor 1})&=\frac{8}{27}\end{align*}$$
